full_judgment:
Mahmudul Hoque J: In this application under Article 102 of the Constitution of Bangladesh a Rule Nisi was issued at the instance of the Petitioners calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the Order No.58 dated 29-7-2012 as evidenced by Annexure-F passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet in Artha Jari Case No. 16 of 2005 refusing the Petitioners' prayer for adjustment of their deposit against the outstanding loan and directing the Decree-Holder Respondent No.3 to supply the draft copy of auction sale should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect, and as to why his earlier Order No. 54 dated 29-2-2012 as evidenced by Annexure-E, directing the Decree-Holder Respondent No. 3 to adjust the deposit made by the Petitioners in the loan account of the borrower judgment-debtors should not be restored and/or such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts leading to disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the Petitioners are full brothers and they have purchased 0.1155 acre of land in Plot Nos. 9094/11422, 9095/11423 appertaining to Khatian Nos. 2951/3, 2951/4 corresponding to Settlement Khatian No. 2951 of Mouza Sylhet Municipality by two registered sale deeds being Nos. 12503 and 12504 dated 17-7-2005 from the Respondent Nos. 5 to 12. The petitioners subsequently came to know that the said property was mortgaged by the Respondent Nos. 5 to 12 in favour of Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation ("HBFC"), Sylhet, who had defaulted in paying the loan money. HBFC filed Artha Rin Suit being No. 51 of 1992 which was decreed in its favour. The said Decree-Holder HBFC for realization of its decretal amount filed Artha Jari Case No. 16 of 2005. Thereafter, the petitioners after getting information about the aforesaid case sent a legal notice to the Respondent Nos. 5 to 12 for alleged suppression of fact and to take necessary steps for releasing the property from HBFC. Subsequently the Respondent Nos. 5 to 12 after receipt of the said notice, instead of taking any steps for releasing the property, filed Title Suit No. 185 of 2006 against the petitioners in the 2nd Court of the Joint District Judge, Sylhet, for declaration that the kabalas registered in favour of the petitioners in respect of the aforesaid property are forged and fraudulent and for recovery of khas possession of the said property

3. Thereafter, the petitioners filed an application for addition of party as judgment-debtors in the Artha jari Case with a prayer for accepting the decretal amount from the petitioners. But the Respondent Nos. 5 to 12 filed an objection and the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat by its Order dated 14-11-2006 rejected the application of the petitioners and published Tender Notice for auction sale of the property in the daily 'Sabuj Sylhet' on 4-3-200. Impugning the said Order and the Tender Notice the Petitioner No. 1 filed Writ Petition No. 2782 of 2007 in this Court in which a Rule Nisi was issued and Order was passed staying operation of the Impugned Notice for auction. However, by this Court's Order dated 26.05.2010 the Rule was discharged for non-prosecution on the assurance of the Respondent No. 5, the Borrower-Judgment-Debtor, that she will repay the entire outstanding loan within a short period. Subsequently, the Respondent Nos. 5 to 12 did not act as per their assurance and deposit the decretal money. However, by Order dated 21-7-2011 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat the Petitioners were added as judgment-debtors Nos. 2 and 3 in the Artha Jari Case.

4. That on an Order of the Artha Rin Adalat ("Adalat") the Petitioners have deposited Taka 20,44,000 (Twenty lakh, forty four thousand) in the account of the Respondent No. 4 HBFC towards adjustment of the outstanding loan owed by the Respondents Nos. 5 to 12 vide three deposit receipts, one dated 28-3-2007 and other two dated 20-7-2011.

5. That on 12-1-2012 the petitioners as the added judgment-debtors filed an application in the Adalat praying for a direction to the Decree-Holder HBFC for adjustment of the deposit made by the petitioners in the loan account of the Borrower-judgment-debtors, the Respondent Nos. 5 to 12. By Order No. 54 dated 29-2-2012 the Adalat allowed the application of the Petitioners with the consent of the Respondent No. 3 and Respondents Nos. 5 to 12, directing the HBFC to adjust the amount deposited by the Petitioners in the loan account of the Borrower-judgment-debtors.

6. That on 9-7-2012 HBFC filed an application for reviewing the Order No. 54 dated 29-2-2012. The Adalat by Order No. 58 dated 29-7-2012 reversed its earlier Order and directed the HBFC to supply draft copy of auction sale by 13-8-2012 holding that the Borrower-judgment-debtors denied the claim of the Petitioners to have purchased the case land from them and that the higher authority within HBFC refused to adjust the deposit against the outstanding loan. At this juncture the Petitioners moved this Court by filing this application under Article 102 of the Constitution challenging the propriety of the impugned order and obtained the present Rule and Order of Stay.

7. By filing a supplementary affidavit the Petitioners further stated that Toslimunnessa, the Respondent No. 5 and her son Mohiuddin Ahmad, the Respondent No. 12, and daughter Yasmin Akhtar took loan from Uttara Bank, Ambarkhana Branch, Sylhet by mortgaging 0.070 acre of land covered by SA Plot No. 9095/11423, corresponding to BS Plot No. 7108. Out of the said land Toslimunnessa sold 0.035 acre of land by a kabala dated 18-5-2005 to Md. Mostafa Ahmad (Azad), who in turn sold the same to the Petitioners by kabala No. 12503 dated 17-7-2005. Toslimunnessa and her sons and daughters, the Respondents Nos. 5-12 herein, sold .08 acre of land to the Petitioners by kabala No. 12504 dated 17-7-2005 suppressing the fact of earlier mortgage with the Uttara Bank. The Respondents Nos. 5-12 defaulted in payment of loan and the said Bank filed Artha Rin Suit No. 7 of 2008 in the 2nd Court of the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet. The Suit was decreed, and the decree-holder Bank filed Artha Rin Execution Case No. 28 of 2009 for realization of the decretal money through auction sale of the mortgaged property under sections 33(1) and (4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 ("Act"). Since, there was no bid in response to sale proclamations and notices, on the application of the said Bank the Adalat issued and registered a certificate of title on 01-8-2012 in respect of the aforesaid 0.070 acre of land in favour of the Bank under section 33(7) of the Act declaring the title of the said land vested in the decree-holder Bank. The present Petitioners made representations to Uttara Bank on 7-6-2012 and 27-2-2013 seeking release of 0.035 acre of land, which the Petitioners purchased from Md. Mostafa Ahmad Azad, a transferee from Toslimunnessa Jaigirdar on 17-7-2005, on receipt of the decretal amount from the Petitioners. But instead of responding to the Petitioners, Uttara Bank published auction notice on 28-4-2013 for sale of 0.07 acre of land. The present Petitioners challenged the same by filing Writ Petition No. 4924 of 2013. By an Order dated 15-5-2013 this Court directed the said Bank to dispose of those representations of the Petitioners within a period of one month in accordance with law and further directed that till disposal of those representations the auction process initiated by the Bank be kept in abeyance.

8. Uttara Bank, however, remaining in non-compliance of that Order, the present Petitioners, consequentially filed Contempt Petition No. 74 of 2014 wherein a Rule was issued on 15-5-2014 directing the Uttara Bank to show cause as to why a contempt proceeding will not be drawn against it. This led to a positive response from the Bank manifested in its recognition that the Petitioners should pay the whole of the decretal amount and take whole of the land. Ultimately, the Petitioners agreed to the Bank's proposal to secure their property and the said Bank by a kabala executed and registered on 9-6-2014 sold the land in the case plot No. 9095/11423 to the Petitioners who thus acquired title in the said land.

9. Evident also is the fact that, Toslimunnessa Jaigirdar took loan of Taka 5,00,000 from the Islami Bank Bangladesh Ltd. Ambarkhana Branch by mortgaging the self same land by a deed of mortgage dated 21-7-2002 prior to the Petitioners' acquisition of the said land from her. Thereafter, the Petitioners got the property released by paying the loan and then took the kabala No. 12504 dated 17-7-2005 from Toslimunnessa Jaigirdar and her son and daughter. At the time of purchase, the vendors handed over certified copy of their title deed to the Petitioners on the plea that the original had been lost. The Petitioners further asserted that, if the money paid by the Petitioners is adjusted in the account of the judgment-debtors, the Petitioners undertake that they would not demand from HBFC return of the original title deeds of the Borrower-judgment-debtors and will not claim any other right of subrogation.

10. HBFC contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition denying all the material allegations made in the application contending, inter alia, that on an Order of the Adalat the Petitioners deposited the decretal money in their names and not in the names of the Borrower-Judgment-Debtor Respondent Nos. 5-12. Since the higher authority within HBFC refused to accept the said deposit in the names of the Petitioners, HBFC filed a petition in the Adalat on 9-7-2012 to review the Order No. 54 passed by it on 29-2-2012 and the Adalat by Order No. 58 dated 29-7-2012 reversed the earlier Order and directed HBFC to supply draft copy of auction sale by 13-8-2012. It is also contended that HBFC cannot accept the decretal amount from a third party other than judgment-debtors as there is no legal relationship between HBFC and the Petitioners. Rather there is a title dispute between the judgment-debtors and the Petitioners relating to the mortgaged property. So, the Petitioners have no locus standi and, as such, the Writ Petition is not maintainable and the Rule is liable to be discharged.

11. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, the learned Advocate appearing for the Petitioners submit that the Petitioners as purchasers with a view to save the property from auction filed an application in the Artha Jari Case praying for addition of party as judgment-debtors and accepting the decretal amount from the Petitioners. By Order dated 21-7-2011 the Adalat added the Petitioners as Judgment-Debtor Nos. 2 and 3 in the Artha Jari case. The respondents did not challenge the said Order before the higher court and, as such, the Petitioners have assumed the status of judgment-debtors co-extensive with the Respondent Nos. 5 to 12. As judgment-debtors the Petitioners in pursuance of an Order of the Adalat dated 29-12-2012 have deposited entire decretal amount with interest totaling Taka 20,44,000 in the account of HBFC towards adjustment of the loan owed by the Respondent Nos. 5-12. The Adalat passed the said Order with the consent of HBFC and Respondent Nos. 5-12 directing HBFC to adjust the amount in the loan account of the Respondent Nos. 5-12. On an application filed by HBFC the Adalat reversed the Order No. 54 dated 29-2-2012 and directed the Decree-Holder to supply draft copy of the auction notice by 13-8-2012 most illegally and arbitrarily. Mr. Maswood further submits that the Artha Rin Adalat cannot review its Order passed earlier which has already taken effect. It is also argued that any person whose interest is involved in the mortgaged property other than a Judgment-Debtor is similarly legally entitled to pay and satisfy the decree with a view to get the property released. Since, therefore, the Petitioners have assumed the role of judgment-debtors in the Artha Jari Case by way of addition, there is no legal impediment in they making the payment of the decretal amount towards adjustment of the loan of the Respondent Nos. 5 to 12. It is argued, therefore, that, the Adalat passed the Order on 29-2-2012 rightly allowing the Petitioners prayer to pay the amount and directing HBFC to adjust the same in the loan account of the loanee.

12. The arguments above are predicated on the core submission of Mr. Maswood that person other than the judgment-debtor can satisfy the decretal amount and seek recording of satisfaction of the decree as per provisions of Order XXI, rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure ("Code"). Accordingly, the Petitioners having made payment of the decretal amount to the Decree-holder, the latter is legally bound to adjust the same in the account of the borrower judgment-debtor. But the Decree-Holder HBFC instead of making adjustment of the amount in the account of the loanee with a mala fide intention, Mr Maswood submits, sought review of the Order passed by the Adalat. It is also argued that the intention of the legislature is to recover money from the borrower judgment-debtor and not to sell the property of the mortgagor or their successor. But in the instant case HBFC is more interested to sell the property in auction than to adjust the amount paid by the Petitioners in the account of the Respondent Nos. 5-12 borrowers. Such-attitude and action of the HBFC has got no legal sanction under the Act or under any other laws and, as such, the impugned order passed by the Adalat reversing its earlier Order is palpably illegal and without lawful authority. It is also submitted that the Petitioners shall not claim redemption of the mortgaged property in their favour or insist on the handing over of the original property documents, if the adjustment of the money is made by HBFC in the loan account of the judgment-debtors. In support of his submissions he has referred to the case of KS Hussain Peer vs Kadapala Venkata Ramana Reddy reported in AIR 1989 (AP) 62.

13. Mr Imam Hossain with Ms Khurshid Jahan, the learned Advocates appearing for the Respondent No. 4 submit that the Petitioners are neither mortgagors nor judgment-debtors as such they are not entitled to make payment of the decretal amount to HBFC which is not legally obliged to accept the payment made by them and to release the mortgage property in favour of any person other than the mortgagors. Mr Imam also submits that there is a dispute between the mortgagor-borrower and the Petitioners regarding validity of the sale deeds alleged to have been executed by the mortgagors. If the payment is received from the Petitioners and the property is released by HBFC, there is the risk of multiplicity of proceedings and anticipating such scenario HBFC refused to accept the payment and adjust the same in the account of the borrower and took step for auction sale as per Order of the Adalat. It is also argued that the Artha Rin Adalat can rectify its own order under section 57 of the Act and there is no illegality in the impugned order. In support of his submissions he has referred to the case of Md Salim Hossain vs Uttara Bank Ltd. reported in 17 BLC (AD) 154, facts of the present case is different from the case referred to by the Respondent's counsel.

14. Heard the learned Advocates for the parties, perused the writ petition, supplementary affidavit, Affidavit-in-Opposition along with the Annexures annexed thereto.

15. In the present case the Petitioners grievance stems from the Order No. 58 dated 29-7-2012 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet reversing its order No. 54 dated 29-2-2012 by which the Court directed the Decree-Holder HBFC to adjust the amount deposited by the Petitioners in the loan account of the borrower judgment-debtors. For proper appreciation, Order No. 54 is reproduced below;

৫৪। ২৯-২-১২ অদ্য অত্র মোকদ্দমা শুনানীর জন্য দিন ধার্য্য। ডিক্রিদার পক্ষ হাজিরা দিয়াছেন। দায়িক পক্ষ হাজিরা দিয়াছেন। দায়িক পক্ষ হাজিরা দিয়াছেন। নথি শুনানীর জন্য লওয়া হইল।

Heard the petition filed by added judgment-debtors seeking for an order directing the decree holder bank to adjust the amount deposited by them in the loan account of the borrower judgment-debtor. Ld. Lawyer for decree holder bank and also the Ld. Lawyer for the borrower judgment-debtor did not oppose the prayer. Obviously, the Petitioners deposited the decretal amount in the concerned loan account of the borrower judgment-debtor unassumingly and they look forward to having their dispute settled in T.S. 185/06. On the other hand, borrower judgment-debtors have resorted to dilatory tactics turning down their commitment made before the Hon'ble High Court Division in Writ Petition No 2782/07 and have filed petition seeking for adjournment. Again today Considering every aspect, the prayer of the added judgment-debtors be allowed and that of the borrower judgment-debtors be rejected. Decree holder is directed to adjust the amount deposited by the added Judgment-debtors according to the date of such deposit and submit report by 9-4-12 as to their satisfaction."

16. From a perusal of the above quoted Order of the Adalat, it is found that the direction given by the Adalat to adjust the amount deposited by the Petitioners in the account of the borrower-judgment-debtor without any objection from the decree-holder as well as the judgment-debtors i.e. Respondent Nos. 5 to 12. Thereafter, HBFC by filing an application on 9-4-2012 prayed three months' time to effect adjustment of the amount and for an Order enabling HBFC not to hand over the original documents to the added judgment-debtor-petitioners. The Adalat allowed time as prayed for and fixed 9-7-2012 for further Order. On the date fixed the HBFC filed an application under Order 47, rule 1 of the Code for review of the Order No. 54 dated 29-2-2012. The Court fixed 12-7-2012 and thereafter on 29-7-2012 for hearing the said application. The Adalat heard the application filed by HBFC on 29-7-2012 and upon hearing the parties allowed the application and accordingly reversed its earlier Order dated 29-2-2012 in the terms which runs thus:-

"58. 29-7-12 today is fixed for hearing of both the Petitions filed by the contending parties and order. Both parties filed hazira. Heard the ld. Lawyers at length and perused the petition with inept attention along with the record as a whole. As per version of the petition propounded by the decree holder, higher authority of the decree holder declines to adjust the amount deposited by the added judgment-debtors. Obviously, 'the added judgment-debtors have deposited the entire dues of the impugned loan disclosing that they purchased the scheduled property in good faith from the borrower-judgment-debtors by virtue of the kabalas dated 17-7-05 but the borrower judgment-debtors headed by Toslimunnessa Jaigirdar denied such claim stating that the deeds are forged and were procured from her under threat. It is further asserted that she has already instituted T.S. 185/06 praying for cancellation of the kabalas. In such state of affair, higher authority of the decree holder logically refuses to adjust the amount deposited by the added judgment-debtors to avoid further complicacy.

Banking upon foregoing observations, I could not but accept the apprehension of the decree-holder and entertain his prayer. Hence the prayer is allowed. Ipso facto the prayer of the added judgment-debtor is rejected, especially when their review petition has been disposed of by the Head Office of the decree holder with negation. Hence, in view of order No. 40 Decree-holder is directed to supply draft copy of auction sale by 13-8-12."

17. The impugned order above raises the core issue for this Court's consideration thus: Can a person other than the Judgment-debtor pay or satisfy the decretal amount in the account of the Judgment-debtor and whether the Adalat is empowered to review an earlier Order?

18. To answer the first part of the question raised, provisions of payment under decree provided under Order XXI, rules 1 and 2 of the Code may be looked into. These run thus:-

19. Order XXI R.1. Modes of paying money under decree—(1) All money payable under a decree shall be paid as follows, namely:-

(a) by deposit in or by postal money order sent to the Court whose duty it is to execute the decree, or

(b) out of Court to the decree-holder, or

(c) otherwise as the Court which made the decree directs.

2(a) where any payment is made under clause (a) of sub-rule (1), notice of such payment shall be given to the decree-holder or the person in whose favour the order is made.

(b) The cost of giving such notice shall be borne by the person making payment who shall have the option of having the notice served either by a process-server of the Court or by registered post. No such notice shall issue until the said cost shall have been paid.

Order XXI, r-2—Payment out of Court to decree-holder. (1) where any money payable under a decree of any kind is paid out of Court, or the decree is otherwise adjusted in whole or in part to the satisfaction of the decree-holder, the decree holder shall certify such payment or adjustment to the Court whose duty it is to execute the decree, and the Court shall record the same accordingly.

(2) The judgment-debtor also may inform the Court of such payment or adjustment, and apply to the Court to issue a notice to the decree-holder to show cause, on a day to be fixed by the Court, why such payment or adjustment should not be recorded as certified; and if, after service of such notice, the decree-holder fails to show cause why the payment or adjustment should not be recorded as certified, the Court shall record the same accordingly.

(3)A payment or adjustment which has not been certified or recorded as aforesaid, shall not be recognized by any Court executing the decree.

20. It is to be noted that Order XXI, rule I deals with diverse modes of payment of the decretal amount. In that regard, payment can be made by deposit into the Court, out of the Court to the decree-holder or otherwise as the Court directs. The intention of the legislature is to realize the decretal amount by the decree-holder by putting the decree in execution. It is to be deduced, therefore, that the decree-holder is concerned with the payment of the decretal amount whatever be the source for such payment. In that regard, if any person comes forward to pay the decretal amount on behalf of the judgment-debtor or such person is obliged to pay the decretal amount due to various circumstances the decree-holder, in this Court's view, instead of refusing such payment should come forward to accept the payment.

21. In the present case the situation is that the Petitioners are constrained to pay the decretal amount in the account of the judgment-debtor to protect their property from auction sale and they, for such reason, came forward to satisfy the decree by making payment to the decree-holder with a view to safeguard them from resultant loss and further harassment and hardship. Order XXI, rule (2)(1) of the Code obliges the decree-holder to certify such payment or adjustment of the decretal amount to the Court but the decree-holder HBFC in the present case refused to accept and adjust the amount paid by the Petitioners in the account of judgment-debtors. Instead, HBFC got the earlier positive and favourable direction of the Adalat to adjust the amount paid by the Petitioners in the account of the judgment-debtor reviewed.

22. A cumulative reading of the clauses (a)(b) and (c) of rule 1 coupled with rule 2 of Order XXI of the Code reveals that while judgment-debtors are legally bound to pay the decretal amount to the Decree Holder, there is little indication as who specifically may pay the amount in the manner formulated in clause (b) of Sub-rule 1. This, in this Court's view, sufficiently envisage a scenario where a person who has purchased the property subject to the encumbrances may step into the shoes of the vendor and, though not being the borrower Judgment-Debtor strictly understood, by that reason is entitled to, and not precluded from, pay the decretal amount. Indeed, this can be seen substantiated from another perspective for example, under Section 55(5)(d) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 which runs thus:-

55. Rights and liabilities of buyer and seller—In the absence of a contract to the contrary, the buyer and the seller of immovable property respectively are subject to the liabilities, and have the rights, mentioned in the rules next following, or such of them as are applicable to the property sold:

(5) The buyer is bound—

(d)—Where the ownership of the property has passed to the buyer, as between himself and the seller, to pay all public charges and rent which may become payable in respect of the property, the principal moneys due on, any encumbrances subject to which the property is sold, and the interest thereon afterwards accruing due'.

23. This Court finds, therefore that given the above quoted provisions of law, a buyer shall be bound to pay the moneys due on any encumbrances subject to which the property is sold and the interest thereon afterwards accruing due. In the instant case the Petitioners contend to have purchased the case property with the encumbrances and, as such, they suffer from no legal impediment to pay the decretal amount as public charge to the decree-holder to satisfy the decree even given the fact that the fact of mortgage is not disclosed in the sale and notwithstanding the pending of Title Suit No. 185 of 2006. It is understood that the sale in question took place subject to encumbrances. For that reason also the Petitioners can pay and satisfy the decree as alleged purchaser of the property subject to a mortgage.

<u>24. Furthermore, Order XXI, rule 2 of the Code also does not preclude or prohibit any person to apprise the Court regarding payment and record satisfaction of the decree. This Court, accordingly, finds no rationale or purpose behind the rigid interpretation of disabling the judgment-debtor or the Petitioners to set in motion the proceeding for recording satisfaction of the decree. Indeed, there is no prejudice to the Decree Holder if any person whatever may seek satisfaction of the decree on proof of payment of the decretal amount in the account of the judgment-debtors as provided under Order XXI, rule 1. Given these facts and circumstances, it is this Court's view that Order XXI, rule 1 of the Code does not indeed preclude person(s) other than Judgment-Debtor(s) to pay the decretal amount in the name of the Judgment-Debtor(s) and seek a recording of such satisfaction of decree accordingly.</u>

25. To answer the second part of the question earlier raised, this Court, upon visiting the Act in its entirety has found nothing therein that attests .to the fact of the Artha Rin Adalat being empowered to review its own Orders. By that reason, and given the observations herein above, this Court finds that the impugned order on the face of it is illegal and not sustainable in law. Therefore, this Court finds merit in the Rule and is inclined to make the Rule absolute. However, nothing of this judgment shall affect the merit of the Title Suit No. 185 of 2006 filed by the Respondent Nos. 5-12 against the petitioners challenging the validity of the sale deeds in question.

26. In the result the Rule is made absolute, however, without any order as to costs.

27. Accordingly, the Order No. 58 dated 29-7-2012 as evidenced by Annexure-F passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet in Artha Jari Case No. 16 of 2005 refusing the Petitioners prayer for adjustment of their deposit against the outstanding loan and directing the decree-holder Respondent No. 4 to supply the draft copy of auction sale is declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect, and the Order No. 54 dated 29-2-2012 as evidenced by Annexure-E, directing the Decree-Holder Respondent No. 4 to adjust the deposit made by the Petitioners in the loan account of the borrower Judgment Debtors is, hereby, restored.

28. The Respondent No.4 decree-holder HBFC is, hereby, directed to adjust the amount paid by the Petitioners in the account of the borrower-judgment-debtors, i.e. Respondent Nos. 5 to 12 and to certify the payment and adjustment of the decretal amount in accordance with law and consequentially release the property in question by way of redemption to the mortgagors.

29. Furthermore, the Artha Rin Adalat is directed to dispose of the case recording satisfaction of the decree after confirming that the payment duly made by the Petitioners in the account of the borrower-judgment-debtor i.e., Respondent Nos. 5 to 12.

30. The Order of stay granted earlier at the time of issuance of the Rule is, hereby, vacated.

Communicate a copy of this judgment at once to the Artha Rin Adalat concerned.

End.

full_judgment:
Mahmudul Hoque J: In this application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh a Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause, why the Impugned Order No. 1 dated 21-11-2005 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 2 at Bagerhat in Artha Jari No. 111, of 2005 whereby issued a warrant of arrest should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts relevant for disposal of the Rule are that:-

Respondent No. 2 Bank instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 9 of 2003 as plaintiff ("Respondent") against the present Petitioners ("Petitioners") as Defendants for realization of loan amounting to Taka 1,11,934. The said suit was decreed against the Petitioners. Thereafter the Respondent Bank as decree holder put the said decree into execution by filing Artha Jari Case No. 17 of 2004. In the said execution case the mortgaged property was placed at auction under sections 33(1) and 33(4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 ("Ain") but no bidders participated in the auction, consequent upon which the Respondent Bank filed an application under section 33(5) of the Ain praying for issuance of a certificate in favour of the Respondent Bank vesting with the right of enjoyment and possession of the mortgaged property. The Artha Rin Adalat by its Order dated 5-4-2005 issued a certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain in favour of the Respondent Bank. The Petitioners after issuance of the certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain filed an application on 11-5-2005 for recalling the said Order dated 5-4-2005. The Artha Rin Adalat upon hearing rejected the same. Subsequently the dispute between the Respondent Bank and the petitioners, as claimed by the Petitioners, came into end by a compromise and on the basis of said compromise the Petitioners have already made payment of all the dues to the Bank. But the Bank decree holder most illegally filed Second Execution Case being Artha Jari Case No. 111 of 2005 against the Petitioners on 21-11-2005 and on the very day of filing this Second Execution Case the Artha Rin Adalat issued warrant of arrest to the Petitioner on the prayer of the decree holder Bank.

3. At this juncture the Petitioners by filing this application challenges the legality and propriety of the said Order and obtained the present Rule and stay.

4. The Respondent Bank contested the Rule by filing Affidavit-in-opposition, Supplementary affidavit-in-opposition denying all the material allegations made by the Petitioners in the application contending, inter alia, that the certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain issued by the Artha Rin Adalat is legal and valid and the decree holder Bank rightly initiated Second Execution proceeding against the Petitioners and the Artha Rin Adalat legally issued warrant of arrest.

5. Mrs Afsana Begum, the learned advocate appearing for the Petitioners submits that the instant Second Execution Case is not maintainable in law because of the fact that the First Execution Case No. 17 of 2004 is still pending and during pendency of the First Execution Case the law does not permit the decree holder to initiate Second Execution Case against the Petitioners. She further submits that admittedly a certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain has been issued by the Court in favour of the decree holder Bank with the right of possession and enjoyment of the property till realization of the decretal amount from the Petitioners. Referring section 33(5) of the Ain she also argued that the law says after obtaining certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain the decree holder Bank ought to have sold the property by auction and adjust the sale proceeds with the decretal amount and in the event of any short fall the decree holder can initiate Second Execution proceeding against the Petitioner-judgment debtors. But in the instant case after obtaining certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain the Bank took no steps for selling the property as per the provision contained in section 33(5) of the Ain. Without selling the property by auction second execution case cannot be filed and, as such, issuance of warrant of arrest against the petitioners by the impugned Order is also palpably illegal on the face of it.

6. Referring section 30 of the Ain, she further submits that after filing of the Second Execution Case, it was incumbent upon the decree holder and the Court to serve notice upon the Judgment-debtor through Process Server as well as through Post Office registered with AD. But the impugned Order shows that no notice as required by law was issued and served upon the Judgment-debtor-Petitioners. Without issuance and service of the notice of filing of the Second Execution Case issuance of warrant of arrest at the instance of the decree holder is illegal and without lawful authority.

7. Mr Md Afzal Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the Respondent No. 2 Bank candidly submits that it is difficult for him to disagree with the provision of law and the submissions made by the Petitioners counsel. However he submits that in issuing W/A the executing court committed no illegality in law.

8. Heard the learned Advocates for the parties, perused the application, Affidavit-in-opposition, Supplementary affidavit-in-opposition along with the Annexures annexed thereto.

9. This Rule stems from the Order dated 21-11-2005 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 2, Bagerhat in Artha jari Case No. 111 of 2005 issuing an Order of warrant of arrest against the Petitioners in a Second Artha Jari Case at the instance of the Respondent Bank. For proper appreciation of the submission made by the learned Advocate for the petitioners it is deemed pertinent to reproduce Order No. 1 in its entirety as reads thus:-

আদেশ নং-০১ তাং-২১-১১-২০০৫

অদকার দাখিলি জারী মামলাটি নতুন নম্বর ও নিবন্ধন করা হউক ৷ ডিক্রিদার পক্ষ ফিরিস্তি লিখিত ভাবে কাগজপত্র দাখিল করিয়াছে উক্ত কাগজ পত্র নথিভুক্ত রাখা হউক ৷ ডিক্রীদারপক্ষ সকল তলবানা দাখিল করিয়াছে ৷ উক্ত তলবানা নথিভুক্ত রাখা হউক ৷ অত্র আদালতের অর্থঋণ জারী ১৭/০৪ নং মামলার ইং ৫-৪-২০০৫ তারিখের অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন ২০০৩ এর ৩৩(৫) ধারামতে ইস্যুকৃত সার্টিফিকেট বুনিয়াদে অত্র জারী মামলা আইন নির্দিষ্ট সময়ের মধ্যে দাখিল করিয়াছে।ডিক্রীদার পক্ষ এ্যাফিডেবিটের পোষকতায় অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন ২০০৩ এর ৫৭ ধারামতে অত্র জারি মামলা গ্রহণের জন্য সত্য পাঠযুক্ত দরখাস্ত দাখিল করিয়াছে ৷ ন্যায় বিচারের স্বার্থে মামলাটি আপাততঃ গৃহীত হইল ৷ ডিক্রীদার পক্ষ অপর একটি দরখাস্ত এ্যাফিডেবিটের পোষকতায় অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন ২০০৩ এর ৩৪ ধারামতে সত্য পাঠযুক্ত একটি দরখাস্ত দ্বারা দরখান্তের বর্নিত কারনে ১নং দায়িকের প্রতি গ্রেফতারী পরোয়ানা ইস্যু করিবার জন্য প্রার্থনা করিয়াছে৷ ডিক্রীদার পক্ষেও দাখিলকৃত গ্রেফতারী পরেয়োনা আবেদন মঞ্জুর করা হইল ৷ আগামী ইং ২২-১-২০০৬ তারিখ ধার্য্য করিয়া দায়িকের প্ৰতি গ্রেফতারী পরোয়ানা ইস্যু করা হউক৷ ধার্য্য তারিখ ২২-১-২০০৬ গ্রেফতারী পরোয়ানা তামিল অন্ত ফেরতের জন্য দিন ধার্য্য রহিল৷

10. From a perusal of the above quoted impugned Order, this Court finds that the Artha Rin Adalat on the very day of filing this execution case, instead of issuing notice through Court and by Post to the Judgment debtor, directly issued warrant of arrest against the Petitioner on the prayer of the Respondent Bank which is absolutely against the provisions of law and violation of mandatory provision contained in section 30 of the Ain. In any proceeding, it is the duty of the Court to issue summons/notices for service of the same upon the Defendant and or Judgment-debtor informing filing of the suit/case and asking them to appear and to file written statements or objections, if there be any. But in the present case, the Artha Rin Adalat took no such step for service of notices upon the Judgment-debtors rather issued warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtor on the very day of filing execution case, most unfortunately ignoring and violating the relevant provisions of law. Apart from this, admittedly, the Respondent Bank obtained a Certificate under section 33(5) of the AM from the Court in an earlier execution case. But the delivery of possession of the property in question has not yet been effected. In the absence of delivery of possession, the earlier Execution Case No. 17 of 2004 shall be deemed to be still pending as indicated in section 33 (7Ka) of the Ain, as subsequently amended in 2010, thinking the necessity of delivery of possession through Court and practicability of the same which reads as follows;

৩৩ (৭ক) উপ-ধারা (৫) বা (৭) এর অধীন সম্পত্তির দখল আদালত যোগে প্রাপ্ত হওয়া আবশ্যক হইলে, ডিক্রীদারেৱ লিখিত আবেদনের ভিত্তিতে আদালত ডিক্রীদারকে উক্ত সম্পত্তির দখল অর্পণ করিতে পারিবে ৷

11. Therefore, during pendency of an Execution Case, the law does not permit the decree holder to initiate a further execution case against the Judgment debtor as per provision of section 33(6) of the Ain. Furthermore, it is incumbent upon the Bank decree holder to sell the property by auction and adjust the sale proceeds with the decretal amount and in the event of any shortfall, the decree holder Bank can proceed with the Second Execution Case as per sub-section (6) of section 33 of the Ain. But in the instant case, the provision of Sub-sections (5) and (6) of section 33 of the Ain has not been complied with by the Respondent Bank. Furthermore, without compliance of the provision of sub-section (5) and (6) of section 33 of the Ain as it appears from the instant case, the decree holder Bank most unfortunately initiated the Second Execution Case against the Petitioner and very interestingly, the Artha Rin Adalat, on the very day of filing Second Execution Case without issuing any notice for service upon the Judgment-debtors violating the provisions of law as well as principle of natural justice as endorsed by our Appellate Division directly issued warrant of arrest against the present Petitioners.

12. For proper appreciation of the question raised by the Petitioners Counsel the provisions in sections 30(1), 33 (5) and (6) of the Ain may be looked into as it was then which run thus:-

৩০ ৷ নোটিশ জারী সম্পর্কিত বিধান (১) আপাততঃ বরবৎ অন্য কোন আইনে যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, ডিক্রীদার আদালতের জারীকারক কর্তৃক এবং প্রাপ্তি স্বীকারসহ রেজিট্রিকৃত ডাকযোগে প্রেরণের নিমিত্তে, জারীর দরখাস্তের সহিত নোটিশ জারীর জন্য সমুদয় তলবানা আদালতে দাখিল করিবেন, এবং আদালত অবিলম্ব উহাদের একযোগে জারীর ব্যবস্থা করিবেন, এবং যদি সমন ইস্যুর ১৫(পনের) দিবসের মধ্যে জারী হইয়া ফেরত না আসে, অথবা তৎপূর্বেই বিনা দাবীতে ফেরত আসে, তাহা হইলে আদালত, উহার পরবর্তী ১৫(পনের) দিবসের মধ্যে বাদীর খরচায় যে কোন একটি বহুল প্রচারিত বাংলা জাতীয় দৈনিক পত্রিকায়, এবং তদুপরি ন্যায় বিচাবের স্বার্থে প্রয়োজনীয় মনে করিলে স্থানীয় একটি পত্রিকায়, যদি থাকে, বিজ্ঞাপন প্রকাশের মাধ্যমে নোটিশ জারী করাইবেন, এবং অনুরুপ জারী আইনানুগ জারী মর্মে গণ্য হইবে ৷

৩৩ ৷ নিলাম বিক্রয়-

(২) ...........................

(৫) কোন সস্পত্তি উপ-ধারা (১), (২), (৩) ও (৪)- এর বিধান অনুসারে বিক্রয় করা সম্ভব না হইলে, উক্ত সম্পত্তি, ডিক্রীকৃত দাবী পরিপূর্ণভাবে পরিশোধিত না হওয়া পর্যন্ত, দখল ও ত্যাগের অধিকারসহ ডিক্রীদারের অনুকূলে ন্যস্ত করা হইবে, এবং ডিক্রীদার উপ-ধারা (১), (২), (৩) ও(৪)-এর বিধান অনুসারে উক্ত সম্পত্তি বিক্রয় করিয়া অপরিশোধিত ডিক্রীর দাবী আদায় করিতে পারিবে, এবং আদালত ঐ মর্মে একটি সার্টিফিকেট ইস্যু করিবে।

(৬) ডিক্রীকৃত অংকের অতিরিক্ত অর্থ বিক্রয় বাবদ আদায় হইলে, উক্ত অতিরিক্ত অর্থ দায়িককে ফেরৎ প্রদান করিতে হইবে, এবং বিক্রীকৃত অর্থ ডিক্রীর দাবী অপেক্ষা কম হইলে অবশিষ্ট অর্থ বাবদ, ২৮ ধারার বিধান সাপেক্ষে, আরো জারীর মামলা গ্রহণযোগ্য হইবে।

13. The said provision of section 33(6) has undergone an amendment by way of addition of Sub-sections (6Ka) and (6Kha) vide "Artha Rin Adalat (Amendment) Act, 2010" (Act No. 16 of 2010), which runs as follows;

(৬ক) উপ-ধারা (৫) ও (৬) এর বিধানে যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, যেক্ষেত্রে কোন সম্পত্তি, দখল ও ত্যাগের অধিকারসহ, ডিক্রীদারের অনুকূলে ন্যস্ত কর সত্বেও ডিক্রীদার উক্ত সম্পত্তি উপযুক্ত মূল্যে প্রকাশ্য নিলামে বিক্রয় করিতে অসমর্থ হন, সেক্ষেত্রে উক্ত সম্পত্তির নির্ধারিত মূল্য কিংবা যুক্তিসংগত আনুমানিক মূল্য বাদ দিয়া, ধারা ২৮ এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, জারীর মামলা দায়ের করা যাইবে৷

(৬খ) এই ধারায় ভিন্নতর যাহা কিইে থাকুক না কেন, উপ-ধারা (৫) এর অধীন কোন সম্পত্তি, দখল ও ভোগের অধিকারনহ্, ডিক্রীদারের অনুকূলে ন্যস্ত হ্ইবার ক্ষেত্রে, অনুরুপ ন্যস্ত হইবার ৬(ছয়) বৎসরের মধ্যে উপ-ধারা (৭)এর অধীন ডিক্রীদারের পক্ষে আদালতের নিকট লিখিত আবেদন করিয়া উক্ত সম্পত্তির মালিকানা আঃনি করা যাইবে এবং তাহা না করা হইলে ৬(ছর) বৎসর উত্তীর্ণ হইবার সাথে সাথেই উক্ত সম্পত্তিতে ডিক্রীদারের মালিকানা স্বয়ংক্রিয়ভাবেই বর্তিত হইবে এবং সংশ্লিষ্ট আদালত হইতে তৎমর্মে ঘোষণা না সনদ গ্রহণ করা যাইবে৷

14. From a perusal of the above quoted sections of the Ain, this Court finds that in every proceeding under this law, issuance of notice for service upon the defendant or opposite party is mandatory under section 30(1) of the Ain and in the event of issuance of a certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain vesting the right of possession and enjoyment with the decree holder, it is incumbent upon the certificate holder to sell the property by auction and to adjust the sale proceeds with the decretal amount and in the event of any shortfall the decree holder can proceed with the Second Execution Case for realization of the remaining claim, as provided in section 33(6) of the Ain.

15. In the instant case, this Court finds that the decree holder Bank as well as the Artha Rin Adalat, in violation of the said provisions of law, proceeded with the Second Execution Case and issued warrant of arrest without issuance of any notice to the Petitioner. The Learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat in this Court's considered view (and being aware of the propriety in not casting aspersion) has failed to show that he has rudimentary knowledge about the laws in general and the Artha Rin Adalat Ain in particular. Resultantly, the impugned Order as well as the proceeding in Artha Jari Case No. 111 of 2005 is found to be illegal and absolutely contrary to the provisions of law.

16. Subsequent amendment made incorporating Sub-sections (6Ka) and (6Kha) provided two scenarios;

a) In the event of failure of the Certificate holder in selling the property at an appropriate price by auction in that case by deducting the determined price of the property or a reasonable price the decree holder can file further execution case subject to the provision of section 28 of the Ain.

b) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law the decree holder may apply before the court within 6 years praying for a certificate of title under section 33(7) of the Ain and in the absence of such application with the expiry of 6 years the title of the property shall automatically vest in the decree holder and a certificate to that effect can be obtained from the court by the decree holder.

<u>17. In both the occasions there are some specific provisions to be followed by the holder of certificate, issued under section 33(5) before proceeding with the Second Execution case, but the Respondent Bank has not followed those provisions in the present case.</u>

<u>18. The entire process of consideration of the Petitioners application variously beginning with the issuance of Certificate under section 33 (5) of the Ain continuing through the filing of a Second Execution case and culminating in the Impugned Order No. 1 dated 21-11-2005 appears to be tainted by a level of high arbitrariness which amounts to illegality. Failure of the Respondent Bank to follow up the provision of section 33(5), (6) and the Adalat failure to follow up the provision of section 30(1) of the Ain appears to be the fatal flow that appears evidently on record.</u>

19. Taking into consideration the above, this Court finds that the impugned Order to be seriously wanting in legal insufficiency and devoid of any judicial satisfaction of relevant applicable laws and principles and thereby to be shorn of all validity and legal effect.

20. Accordingly, this Court hereby declares the impugned order as well as the proceedings in Execution Case No. 111 of 2005 passed and initiated by the Respondents to be illegal and without lawful authority and sets aside the same. In the light of the observation made above this Court finds merit in the Rule issued.

21. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. However, without any order as to costs.

22. The Impugned Order No. 1 dated 21-11-2005 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 2 Bagerhat in Artha jari case No. 111 of 2005 as well as the proceedings in said execution case are hereby declared to have been passed and initiated without lawful authority.

23. The Order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule and extended from time to time is hereby recalled and stand vacated. Let a copy of this Judgment be sent to the Secretary, Ministry of law to note comments made above in the ACR of Mr Md Nazrul Islam Howlader the then Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, court No. 2, Bagerhat.

Communicate a copy of the judgment and order to the Court concerned for information and necessary action.

End.

full_judgment:
Amirul Islam Chowdhury, J: This Rule at the instance of defendant-petitioner was issued on the plaintiff opposite parties to show cause as to why the order dated 104 1990 passed by the Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No.141 of 1985, should not be set aside or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts leading to this revisional application, in short, are as under:

The opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 141 of 1985 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in the suit land. The suit was ultimately decreed ex-parte on 9.11.85. Thereafter the defendant petitioner filed two applications and the said applications were registered as Miscellaneous Case Nos. 4 of 1986 and 12 of 1986 and the said Miscellaneous Cases were heard analogously and dismissed by the trial Court on 20.12.88 Thereafter the defendant petitioner preferred 2 Miscellaneous Appeals in this cowl being Miscellaneous Appeals Nos. 336 of 1988 and 17 of 1989. During pendency of the Miscellaneous Appeals in this court, the original plaintiff respondent No. 2 died on 20.3.90. On an application, filed by the defendant petitioner, the heirs of plaintiff respondent No.2 were substituted in these appeals on 5.1.91. Both the appeals were taken up for hearing analogously and this court by its order dated 5.1.91 allowed the appeals and set aside the ex-parte decree dated 9.11.85. The order of this court was communicated and the L.C. Records were sent down to the trial court and the same were received by the trial court on 25.3.90. Thereafter the heirs of the original plaintiff No. 2 filed an application under order 1 Rule 10 for adding them as plaintiffs in the suit. The suit was originally instituted by 2 plaintiffs, namely plaintiff No. 1 Abdul Karim and plaintiff No.2 Sohala Khatun wife of plaintiff No.1. On the death Sohala Khatun plaintiff No.2, her husband, her sons and others became her heirs and successors-in-interest in respect of the property. On the application filed by the heirs of decesed plaintiff No.2 the trial court allowed the application after hearing of the par ties on 39490 In the meantime the heirs of the de plaintiff No. 2 filed a application for substituting them as decree-holder in the execution case on 18.6.89. But no action could be taken on the application for substitution of the heirs of the deceased plaintiff No.2 as decree holder as stay was granted by: this court in the aforesaid Miscellaneous appeals.

<u>3. Mr. Asrarul Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for defendant petitioner submits that the impugned order' not being in accordance with law is liable to set aside. In this connection Mr. Asrarul Hossain, the learned Advocate for the defendant, referred to Order 22 Rule 3(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure. He also submits that on the death of a party in a proceeding, the heirs of the de-ceased are to be substituted within 90 days from the date of death of the concerned party. In the instant case the concerned plaintiff died on 20.3.89 and as such the application for substitution should have been filed in the trial court within 90 days of the death. He further submits that no application for substitution having been filed, the suit ultimately abated by operation of law and the heirs of the de ceased plaintiff would get another 60 days to filed an application for substitution after set ting aside the abatement. In the instant case, no application for setting aside the abatement was filed within 60 days. Of course, even after 60 days an application could be filed for setting aside the abatement and substituted the heirs, of the deceased party in a suit with an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act In the instant case, Mr. Asrarul Hossain, the learned Advocate for the defendant petitioner further submits that it would be proper for the heirs of the plaintiff No. 2 to file an application for substitution after setting aside the abatement with a prayer for condonation of the delay.</u>

4. In the facts of the instant case, he con cedes that the application for substitution could be allowed. In the circumstances the addition of the heirs of plaintiff No. 2 was not proper. In this connection he referred to the case of Amal Kumar Vs. Mashiur Rahman reported in 30 D.L.R.(AD) 244 and the case of Union if India Vs. Ram Charm reported in AIR 1964 (SC) 215. He also submits that Order 22 Rule 3(2) is applicable in the facts of the instant case.

5. The instant suit merged into the decree and Execution Case being No.66 of 1985 had already been started and an application was filed for substitution of the heirs of the plain tiff decree holder No. 2 in the concerned execution case during the pendency of the afore said Miscellaneous Appeals in this court. In the facts of the instant case it is difficult to say that the concerned suit was still pending in the trial court prior to the disposal of the aforesaid miscellaneous appeals by this court.

6. Mr. Abdur Rahman the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff opposite par ties, submits that the Order 22 Rule 3(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure is applicable in the case of a pending suit but the instant suit was not pending before the trial court. Against the ex-parte decree, the defendant preferred 2 Miscellaneous Appeals against the refusal of the trial court to set aside the ex-parte decree on the applications filed under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure during pendency of the appeals at the instance of the defendant (appellant) the heirs of the deceased plaintiff No. 2 were substituted in the miscellaneous appeals As such he submits that since the heirs of the deceased plaintiff No. 2 were substituted in the appeals there was no necessity for the heirs of the deceased plaintiff No. 2 to take steps for substituting them in the suit inasmuch as the substitution in the appeals would ultimately substitute them in a suit if the miscellaneous appeals are allowed In this connection he has referred to the case of Hema Dibya Vs. Amarendra Kishore Das and others reported in AIR 1966 (Orissa) 55 He further submits that if the limitation for substitution of the heirs of the deceased per son is over, then the heirs could be added in the suit. In this connection he has referred to the case of Rahim Baksha Gazi Vs. Enbar Gazi & others reported in 2. DLR (HC) 500 and the case of Amal Kumar Vs. Mashiur Rahman Reported in 30 DLR (AD) 244 and the case of Mohammadally Tybally and ors. Vs. Safiabar and ors reported in AIR 1940(PC) 215. He also submits that the husband of deceased plaintiff No. 2 is already on record as plaintiff No. 1 and in such case according to the decisions reported in 37 DLR (AD) 85 there is no necessity for substitution Since one of the heirs of the deceased is already on record and according to the decision reported in AIR 1933 (Lahore)765 there is no necessity for setting aside the impugned order by this court

7. In the instant case it appears from the ex-parte decree passed on 9.11.85 that the Miscellaneous Appeals were allowed on 5.1.91. therefore, during the period from 911 85 to 5191 it cannot be said that the suit was pending in the trial court The suit was restored to its original file and number were allowed in the aforesaid Miscellaneous Appeals by this court As such it was not possible during that period to take steps for submitting the heirs of the deceased plaintiff No. 2 in the suit The records of the suit were also called for and kept in this court for disposal of the aforesaid Miscellaneous Appeals The records together with the order of this court for setting aside the ex-parte decree were sent down to the court below and were received by the that court on 25.3.90 The application for addition was filed on 29.3.90 In the circumstances we cannot find that the application has been filed beyond the period of limitation The application has been, filed under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of civil Procedure. It is now well settled that captioning of an application under a provision of law would not debar the court from passing an appropriate order if the court has the power to a pass such an order. In the instant case the application has been filed under Order 1 Rule 10. The application should have been filed for substation under the relevant provision of the Code of Civil Procedure, is under Order 22 Rule 3(2). Since the Court has the power to pass an appropriate order on the application under Order. I Rule 10, we feel that necessary modification of the impugned order is to be made by this Court.

8. In facts and circumstances of the instant case we are of the view that the application under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure be treated as an application under order 22 Rule 3(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure in the facts of the instant case, it is difficult to say that the suit abated due to the non-substituting the heirs of the plaintiff No.2 within 90 design her place. In the facts of the instant case the application filed for substitution in the concerned execution case may be treated as an application for substitution in the suit and allowed. The heirs of the concerned plaintiff are accordingly substituted in the suit

9. With the above modification of the impugned order, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost.

10. We direct the Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka, to the dispose of the suit within 4 months of receipt of this order by the said Court.

End.

full_judgment:
Badrul Haider Chowdhury, J:-This appeal by special leave is directed against the judgment and order in Civil Order No. 39(Ctg.) of 1983 passed by the High Court Division, Chittagong Bench affirming the judgment and decree made by the learned Subordinate Judge in Other Appeal No.149 of 1980 reversing those of the Munsif of the Court of North Raozan, Chittagong in O.S.No.68 of 1976.

2. Plaintiff respondents instituted O.C. Suit No.68 of 1976 in the Court of Munsif at North Raozan against the defendant appellants for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit land. Plaintiffs' case was that Ahmed Ali was the original owner, grand father of defendant No.1. Ahmed Ali sold the suit land to Kala Miah Chowdhury on 29-10-36 for his son Nurul Islam Chowdhury who was a minor. After 9 years Kala Miah Chowdhury sold the suit land to the father of the plaintiff Aminur Rahman on 6-9-1945 by a registered kabala and Nurul Islam Chowdhury after attaining majority executed a deed of relinquishment on 18-2-1952 in favour of the plaintiffs' father. Defendants Nos. 1 to 3 had litigations and enmity. with the plaintiff and they obtained a collusive kabala in favour of defendant No.1 from the said Nurul Islam Chowdhury, defendant No. 4 on 25-4-1967 and threatened the possession of the plaintiffs for which the plaintiffs filed Other Suit No. 105 of 1967 for permanent injunction against the defendants. That suit, however, was dismissed and the appeal preferred against the order of dismissal was also dismissed. The plaintiffs contended that being encouraged by the order of dismissal of the suit and the appeal the defendants dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit land on 22-9-1968 and hence the suit had been filed on 10-5-1976 for confirmation of title and recovery of khas possession.

3. The Trial Court considered that O.S. 105 of 1967 by the plaintiffs' father was a suit for permanent injunction for restraining the defendants from entering upon the suit land and disturbing the plaintiffs' possession. The suit was dismissed by the Trial Court observing:

"As the plaintiff is found to be out of possession, so it is no longer open to him to pray for a decree for permanent injunction."

The order of the dismissal of the suit was also upheld in Other Appeal No.346 of 1968 by the learned District Judge on 21-5-69.

4. In the present suit being O.S. No. 68 of 1976 which was a suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession, the trial court found that the suit land was purchased by Kala Meah Chowdhury in the benami of his one year old minor son out of affection and it was found Nurul Islam Chowdhury was merely benamder of his father. It was also found that the plaintiffs' father got possession of the suit land though title and possession was found in favour of the respondents. The Trial Court then considered the fate of U.S. No. 105 of 1967 while the plaintiff failed to prove his prima facie title and possession and keeping in mind the view of the appellate Court the learned Munsif observed:

"Even though in form this suit is different than the former suit, yet the question of title has already been discussed in the former suit in detail on appeal. So I believe this court has no jurisdiction to decide anything what has already been decided in the former suit on appeal."

5. The appellate Court below considered that this approach was wrong inasmuch as the O.S.No.105 of 1967 was a suit for simply permanent injunction; admittedly there was no final adjudication regarding the title and recovery of khas possession. In the previous suit there was no issue framed regarding puffs title to the suit land. It observed:

"As such I hold that the present suit cannot be barred by res judicata and the Ld. Munsif was not justified in dismissing the suit on the point of res judicata." In this view of the matter the suit was decreed against the defendants appellant.

6. The High Court Division Ins moved in revision and the learned Single Judge dismissed the revisional application summarily by holding that the approach made by the appellate Court below was correct and though the trial court found title to plaintiff it was wrong in dismissing the suit and accordingly upheld the finding of the appellate Court below and dismissed the petition summarily.

7. Leave was granted to consider whether the suit was barred by res judicata inasmuch as the question of title and possession between the parties over the self-same land had allegedly been decided by a competent civil court.

8. In the previous suit O.C. 105 of 1967 plaintiff prayed for permanent injunction. In that suit it was found that the plaintiff failed to prove his possession and the suit was dismissed on that ground alone. The present suit O.C.— 68 of 1976 was a suit for declaration of title and possession, Though the trial Court found in favour of the plaintiff on the issue of title yet dismissed the suit on ground of res judicata. The Appellate Court below considered that the decision in the suit for permanent injunction could not be res judicata in a suit of title and possession.

<u>9. Mr. Siddique Ahmed Chowdhury appearing for the defendants appellants contended that in the suit for permanent injunction, it was found that the plaintiff was not in possess-ion and these findings will operate as res judicata so far possession is concerned. Mr. M. H. Khondker appearing for the plaintiff respondents submitted that the plaintiff was out of possession when the suit for permanent injunction was filed but that would not preclude from bringing a regular suit for title and possession. He has cited a decision of Jail Lal Banduri and others Versus Nanada Chaudhuri and others 18 C.W.N. page 545 where it was held that when the plaintiff is out of possession should not be allowed to sue the defendant who is alleged to he in possession as a trespasser for an injunction. He ought to sue for recovery of the land. This principle was also reiterated in the case of Anila Bala Dasi V. Madhabandhu Narain Roy 46 C.W,N page 20 where it was considered that when plaintiff is out of possession should also pray for recovery of possession in a suit for recovery of title and not merely for injunction. In the case of Bande Ali V. Gokul Misir and others 34 Allahabad 172 a Division Bench after considering the line of decision observed</u>

<u>"We think, however, that the authorities show that a long time it has been accepted in this court and in other High Courts that the of suits of this nature on the ground that the plaintiff is not or has not proved that he is in possession, is no bar to a subsequent suit for possession."</u>

<u>In that case it was considered that the previous suit was a suit for injunction and it was dismissed on the ground that Ike plaintiff was not in possession and it was observed:</u>

<u>"In our opinion no distinction in principle can be drawn between the dismissal of a suit for a declaration of title on the ground that the plaintiff was not in possession, and the dismissal of a suit for an injunction on the same ground".</u>

<u>These long line of decisions were considered in the case of Haji Yar Ali Khan Chowdhury V. Mobarak Ali Chowdhory and others 7 D.L.R. page 6 where it was considered in case where the plaintiff is in possession of the suit property and some body else from outside tries to interfere with his possession, injunction may be a suitable remedy. But where the defendant is in possession, it is wrong to grant a decree for injunction as injunction is a remedy which cannot be utilized for ousting a person from possession who having initially entered into possession in a rightful manner fails to give up possession alter Igor lapse of 16s right. "Where the plaintiff whose right is denied by the defendant is out of possession and the defendant is in possession, the 'further relief' in section 42 of the Specific Relief Act would be recovery of possession and a suit for mere declaration of title without prayer for possession is barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act." In the present case the previous suit as has been stated was a suit for permanent injunction but the present suit was for declaration of title and recovery of possession. Therefore the contention of Mr. Siddique Ahmed Chowdhury does not hold good. Mr. Chowdhury cited 27 D.L.R. 541 in the case of Md. Nur Hossain V. Bangladesh and another wherein the question of res judicata was considered but in that decision the question was considered in the setting namely whether principle of res judicata are applicable When issues are decided in the writ jurisdiction. That decision has no manner of application so far the point involved in this case.</u>

<u>10. Applying these principles there is no hesitation in saying that the appellate Court below was correct in decreeing the suit on merit holding that the previous suit would not operate as res judicata and the High Court Division in dismissing the revisional application has not committed any illegality which warranted interference by this court.</u>

<u>In the result therefore this appeal is dismissed. There will the no order as to costs.</u>

End.

full_judgment:
M. M. Ruhul Amin, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 13.1.92 passed by. Mr. Md. Nurul Islam, Senior Assistant Judge, Jamalpur in O.C. Execution Case No.4 of 1990 should not be set aside or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of this Rule are as follows:

One Kalidas Deb, vendor of opposite party No. 1 instituted a suit for partition in the First Court of Munsi, Jamalpur being Partition Suit No. 148 of 1970 against the predecessors-in-interest of the petitioners and obtained a decree in preliminary form. The said decree was subsequently made final on 25 and the suit was thus finally disposed of.

3. Thereafter the opposite party No. 1 purchased the soil property from the plaintiff Kalidas Deb by a registered kabala dated 2.12.89 The opposite party 1 on 27.3.90 filed O.C. Execution Case No. 4 of 1990 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Jamalpur for execution of the aforesaid final decree dated 25.1.87.

4. Petitioners on 30.5.90 filed written objection in the aforesaid O.C. Execution Case No.4 of 1990 contending inter alia that since the alleged purchase took place during the pendency of the suit she had no locus standi to proceed with the execution of the decrees as she was not a party in the original partition suit No. 148 of 1970 nor did she take any step to be added as a party in the suit. The judgment debtors had already obtained a decree for permanent injunction in respect of the suit property against the plaintiff of Partition Case No. 148 of 1970, and the said decree has subsequently been confirmed by the appellate Court. The execution case is evidently barred by limitation having not been filed within 3 years from the date of final decree.

5. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Jamalpur by his impugned order dated 13.1.92 rejected the objection petition dated 30.5.90 filed by the petitioner and decided to proceed with the execution case.

6. Being aggrieved by the said order the petitioners move this Court and obtained the present Rule. Mr. Gour Gopal Saha, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that in view of the fact that the final decree was made 25.1.87 and the only application for execution of the decree has been filed on 27.3.90 i.e. after the lapse of 3 years 2 months and 3 days it is evident that the execution of the decree is clearly barred under Article 182 of the Limitation Act and as such the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in holding that the execution case is maintainable and the same has resulted in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He next argued that haying regard to the admitted fact that the Execution Case No. 4 of 1990 has been filed after 3 years of the passing of the final decree, it is evidently hit by the provision of Article 182 of the Limitation Act and as such the decree was non executable as being time barred. He further argued that having regard to the fact that since the execution of the decree dated 25.1.87 was never stays by any order of any Court till the filing of the Execution Case No. 4 of 1990 on 27.3.90 and the opposite party was not prevented from starting the execution case within the statutory period of limitation, it's that Section 14 of the Limitation Act is of no avail to the opposite party to avoid the application of Article 182 of the Limitation Act and as such the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in passing the impugned order on an erroneous view of law and the same has resulted in an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice. He lastly argued that the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in passing the impugned order without at all spelling out as to how Section 14 of the Limitation Act could save the apparent time barred decree and the same has resulted in an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice:-

7. Let us quote below the impugned order dated 13.1.1992 passed in Execution Case No. 4 of 1990.

“অদ্য অএ মোকদ্দমা আদেশের জন্য ধার্য আছে। আদেশের জন্য উপস্থাপনা করা হইল। অদ্য ডিক্রিদার পক্ষের বিগত ২৭.০৩.১৯৯০ ইং তারিখের তামাদি আইনের ১৪ ধারার দরখাস্ত এবং  দায়িক পক্ষের ৩০.০৫.১৯৯০ ইং তারিখের আপত্তির দরখাস্ত  আদেশের জন্য গৃহীত হইল। উভয় পক্ষের দরখাস্ত এবং লিখিত আপত্তি এবং বিজ্ঞ এডভোকেট মহোদয়গনের বক্তব্য পর্যালোচনা করিলে দেখা যায় যে, ডিক্রিদার পক্ষের অত্র ডিক্রিদারী মামলাটি আনয়নের ক্ষেত্রে বিলম্বের যথেষ্ট কারণ ছিল। এবং ডিক্রিদার পক্ষে ডিক্রিদারী মামলাটি ৩ বছর ১৯দিন পর আনয়নের ক্ষেত্রে গ্রহণযোগ্য এবং সংগত কারণ বিদ্যমান ছিল বলিয়া আমি মনে করি। এমতাবস্থায় ডিক্রিদার পক্ষের বিগত ২৭-৩-৯০ ইং তারিখে আনীত দরখাস্ত ন্যায় বিচারের স্বার্থে মঞ্জুর করা গেল।

দায়ীক পক্ষ বক্তব্যের সরর্থনে কোন সুস্পষ্ট এবং গ্রহনযোগ্য আইনের উল্লেখ করেন নাই এবং বক্তব্যের সমথের্নে প্রমানীত কাগজাত উপস্থাপন করেন নাই। এমতাবস্থায় দায়ীক পক্ষের আপত্তি অগ্রাহ্য করা হইল।

আগামী ২৫.১.৯২ ইং দিন ধার্য্যে ডিক্রিদার পক্ষকে প্রয়োজনীয় পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণ করিবার জন্যে নির্দেশ দেওয়া গেল।”

<u>8. From the impugned order it is quite clear that the execution case was time barred but the learned Assistant Judge condoned the delay in filing the execution case under section 14 of the Limitation Act. Section 14 of the Limitation Act reads as follows:</u>

<u>"14. EXCLUTION OF TIME OF PROCEEDING BONAFIDE IN COURT WITHOUT JURISDICTION—In computing the period of limitation prescribed for any suit, the time during which the plaintiff has been prosecuting with due diligence another civil proceeding, whether in a Court of first instance or in a Court of appeal, against the defendant, shall be excluded, where the proceeding is founded upon the same cause of action and is prosecuted in good faith in a court which, from defect of jurisdiction, or other cause of a like nature is unable to entertain."</u>

<u>There is no doubt that the provisions of Section 14 of the Limitation Act provides for exclusion of time of proceeding bonafide prosecuted by a party in a Court which has no jurisdiction to entertain the proceeding and this section is available not only to proceedings of the courts of the first instance but also in the appellate Court and in execution courts. But there is nothing on record to show that the decree was put into execution within 3 years in a Court having no jurisdiction to entertain the same. From the impugned order it is quite clear that the decree was apparently barred by limitation and for that reason the learned Assistant Judge condoned the delay under Section 14 of the Limitation Act on an erroneous view of law and as such the same has resulted in an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice. It may be stated here that the present petitioners tiled written objection in the aforesaid O.C. Execution Case No. 4 of 1990 contending inter alia that the execution petition being Lime barred, it is unexecutable.</u>

<u>9. Mr. Saha in support of his contention has placed before me the case of Md. Abdur Rahim and others Vs. Sree Sree Gredhari Jeo reported in 27 DLR 72. in that case the provision of Section 48 of the C.P.C. and Article 182 of the Limitation Act were considered and it was accordingly held:</u>

<u>Both prescribe the period of limitation for the execution of the decree the Civil Procedure Code fixes the longest period whereas the Limitation Act earliest period to take the first step in execution and the subsequent steps known as steps-in-aid."</u>

<u>In that case it was further held that</u>

<u>"Limitation Act prescribes the period of limitation which the decree-holder must take earliest in point of lime for execution, whereas Section 48 of the Code of fixes the maximum limit, but it does not prescribe the time for filing the first application or the subsequent applications for execution. The Limitation Act prescribes that an application for execution is to be made within 3 years from the dates mentioned in third column of Article 182. An application for execution has, therefore to satisfy first, Article 182 of the Limitation Act earliest period prescribed and then also Section 48 of the Code which prescribed the maximum period of Limitation. If the execution petition is hit by any of the two provisions it is to fail."</u>

<u>10. Mr. Saha then placed the case of Bangladesh Jatiya Samabaya Bank Ltd. Vs. Sangbad Daily Paper and others, reported in 35 DLR(AD)5. In that case it is held:</u>

<u>"It is well sewed that 12 years is to be counted from terminus quo mentioned in clauses (a) and (b) of section 48 (I) of the C.P.C. Although the period of 12 years has been fixed which has been termed as an outside period the decree must be kept alive under the Limitation Act and Article 182 requires the first application for execution to the made within 3 years of the decree and each successive application to be made within three years of the final order passed on the last application."</u>

<u>11. There is also nothing on record to show that the decree in question was stayed by any order of any court till the filing of the Execution Case No. 4 of 1990 and as such the opposite party No. 1 was not prevented from starting it during the statutory period of limitation.</u>

12. For the reasons staled above I set aside the impugned order of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Jamalpur dated 13.1.92 passed in O.C. Execution Case No.4 of 1990. The application dated 27.3.90 filed by the judgment in O.C. Execution Case No. 4 of 1990 is allowed.

13. In the result, the Rule is accordingly made absolute without any order as to cost.

End.
